newsitem.title: USA: U.S. JEC chairman criticizes Treasury tax analysis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. JEC chairman criticizes Treasury tax analysis.

text.p: The chairman of the Congressional Joint Economic Committee has asked Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin to use more easily understandable terms when discussing pending tax-law changes.

"Treasury is using a notion of income in its analysis of tax legislation that the overwhelming majority of Americans have never heard of and 99.9 percent of taxpayers do not understand," JEC Chairman Jim Saxton wrote in a letter to Rubin.

Currently, proposals and criticisms are flowing back and forth between Treasury and Capitol Hill on a five-year $85-billion net tax cut bill. Treasury has been critical of many proposals originated by Congress, claiming many of them would leave families worse off.

But Saxton said Treasury was using "an arcane notion" of income that inflates taxpayer income by including items like imputed rent, fringe benefits and other nontaxed items. It has the effect of making many middle-class taxpayers appear to be upper-income earners, he said.
Saxton asked Rubin to provide future analyses of tax proposals based on adjusted gross income, "the same definition of income actually used by taxpayers on their tax returns."

Earlier on Thursday, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers told a Senate subcommittee that the Clinton administration disagreed with several provisions of a tax bill now being considered by the House of Representatives.

Summers claimed the set of proposals drawn up by the tax-writing House Ways and Means committee was needlessly complex. The administration has also complained that it would benefit the well-off at the expense of poorer people.
